title: Minimax ATE Risk in Randomized Trials with Categorical Surrogates and Partial Outcome Validation
banked_reason: D0.5 math referee PASS with no findings; general referee achieved subfield below field floor (paper score ceiling 7.2 < 7.4), salvageable=false.

The publication case also depends on a bounded rather than conclusive historical-priority review, particularly against finite-domain semisupervised mean and off-policy evaluation results.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a matched uniform minimax MSE rate up to universal constants, a computable residual-corrected estimator, fixed-sample lower bounds, the exact o(1/n) phase criterion, and common-calibration rate equivalence. The D0.5 math referee passed with no findings, but the general referee assigned subfield tier below the required field floor and found no in-scope improvement. Formalization did not start; exact constants and a conclusive priority comparison remain open.
tldr: A balanced randomized study contains \(n\) complete treatment--surrogate--outcome records and \(N\) additional treatment--surrogate records, with a binary outcome and \(k\) categorical post-treatment profiles. The note establishes, up to universal constants, the fixed-sample uniform minimax ATE mean squared error rate \(\min\{1,(n+N)^{-1}+\nu/n+\min\{k-1,n\}/n^2\}\) by pairing a computable first-label residual-corrected estimator with fixed-sample lower constructions for surrogate-frequency uncertainty, conditional outcome noise, and unseen deterministic profiles. It proves that risk is \(o(1/n)\) exactly when \(N/n\to\infty\), \(\nu\to0\), and \(k/n\to0\), and that a common outcome-calibration map across arms does not improve the unrestricted global order. The GAIN study motivates costly delayed employment measurement, but its cross-site data fusion is not asserted to obey this exact same-population validation design.
gap: Regular semisupervised mean and surrogate-assisted ATE theory quantifies local residual-variance gains, while finite-action off-policy theory exposes unseen-label risk. The inspected results do not combine an independently enlarged surrogate-frequency sample, a vanishing average conditional-variance budget, arbitrary rare or null profiles, and a rate uniform in the alphabet size.
fill: The estimator uses first observed cell labels only to predict and uses residual correction to remove aggregate imputation bias. Three admissible common-calibration lower subexperiments isolate the three rate terms, yielding the matched benchmark, the exact subparametric phase condition, and the global no-order-gain result for shared calibration.
